overview: Slovakia is a landlocked country in Central Europe. Its capital, Bratislava, lies on the Danube, close to the borders of both Austria and Hungary. Slovakia became independent on 1 January 1993, when Czechoslovakia peacefully split in two. It joined NATO and the European Union in 2004 and uses the euro.

geography.text: Much of Slovakia is mountainous. The Carpathians cross the north and centre of the country, including the High Tatras, the highest range in the Carpathians, which Slovakia shares with Poland. The south-west is lower and flatter, along the Danube, and the country is known for its many caves.

history.text: Slavs settled the area in the 500s, and it was part of Great Moravia before becoming part of the Kingdom of Hungary for about a thousand years. Bratislava, then called Pressburg, was Hungary's capital and coronation city while the Ottomans held Buda. In 1918 Slovakia joined Czechoslovakia, and after a peaceful 'Velvet Divorce' it became independent in 1993.

events.title: Great Moravia
events.text: A Slavic state forms that includes today's Slovakia.

events.title: Capital of Hungary
events.text: Bratislava becomes the capital of the Kingdom of Hungary.

events.title: Czechoslovakia
events.text: Slovaks and Czechs form a joint state.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Slovakia becomes independent after a peaceful split.

government.text: Slovakia is a parliamentary republic. The 150-member National Council chooses the Prime Minister and government, and the President is elected directly every five years. Slovakia joined NATO and the European Union in 2004 and adopted the euro in 2009.

economy.text: Slovakia makes more cars per person than any other country in the world. Volkswagen, Kia, Stellantis and Jaguar Land Rover all have factories there. Electronics, machinery and metals are also important.

culture.text: Slovakia has more castles and castle ruins per person than almost any other country, including the huge Spiš Castle. Its wooden churches in the Carpathian Mountains are listed by UNESCO. Folk music played on the fujara, a long shepherd's flute, is also UNESCO heritage.

items.title: Spiš Castle
items.text: One of the largest castle sites in central Europe.

items.title: Fujara
items.text: A shepherd's flute nearly two metres long.

sport.text: Ice hockey is the most popular sport in Slovakia, and the team won the world championship in 2002. Slovakia is also strong in canoe slalom and skiing; Petra Vlhová won the overall Alpine skiing World Cup in 2021.

items.title: Canoe slalom
items.text: The Hochschorner twins won three Olympic golds in a row.

items.title: Peter Sagan
items.text: Cycling world road race champion three times in a row.
